pairs.difference: A: the ball turns gently from left to right, the highlights are small soft spots on the red and blue panels, and a clean dark cast shadow falls to the right on the sand. B: a broad blown-out white bloom sits on the upper-right white panel, the lower left soaks in red-orange bounce, and the cast shadow is a warm red smear. Its shading range of 0.533 is below the real cards.
pairs.fix: Keep highlights small and soft on each panel, with no large white blown-out patch. Make the shadow on the ball neutral and slightly cool, not red. Lay a clean dark shadow on the sand on one side.

pairs.difference: A: broad even light across the target and bear, the disc shows a simple lit face and darker rim, and shadows on the backboard are gentle. B: a spotlit box with a glow pool behind the target and a heavy vignette dropping into dark corners and a dark lower band. The bear goes muddy at the bottom right, so the light reads as staged rather than as open card light.
pairs.fix: Remove the spotlight pool and dark corners. Light the whole shelf evenly from the upper front, with one soft shadow from the target and the bear onto the back panel.

pairs.difference: A: the unit has a crisp lit top face, a clear cool shadow on the right end cap and a defined window-light shape across the wall. B: the white body is washed in a soft haze with a pale rim all around, the wall has a yellow bloom at left, and the wall shadow is a blurred band. Shading range is low at 0.584 and form contrast high at 0.601.
pairs.fix: Make the top face bright and the right end clearly darker and cooler, with a firm corner between them. Remove the haze and the glow on the wall. Give the wall shadow a defined edge.

pairs.difference: A: strong side light. The lid's right end and the chest's right side fall into deep cool shadow, and the lens shows blue there, matching the real lighthouse and camera. B: even frontal light on all faces, warm shadows in the lens, a soft sun-glow backdrop and little drop between the front and side planes.
pairs.fix: Bring the light from the upper left so the right side of the chest and lid end drop into a deep cool blue-grey shadow. The front stays bright, with a clear jump between the two planes.

pairs.difference: A: open warm light, a soft turn across the white crown and a gentle dark cast shadow right of the visor. B: a dark room with a raking beam, a heavy shadow wedge in the corner, and a peach-lit visor underside in the lens. The shadow on the crown falls off fast into a murky band, and shading range is lower at 0.729.
pairs.fix: Open up the room with bright even daylight and no diagonal shadow wedge on the wall. Turn the white crown softly from light to mid-grey, with one soft dark shadow beside the cap on the floor.

pairs.difference: A: the side and front faces are close in value but a crisp, long dark cast shadow runs left and the base is grounded firmly. B: the left face does drop cooler, but the cast shadow is a faint low smear and the backdrop has a bright glow behind the booth with dark vignetted corners. Grounding is the weak part; the numbers do not separate the two.
pairs.fix: Give the booth a firm dark shadow stretching across the floor to the left, with a dark contact line under the base. Keep the wall evenly lit with no glow behind the booth.

pairs.difference: A: leather-like soft sheen on top, tight dark cast shadows on the floor to the right, and cool violet in the shadow side of the lens. B: bloated glossy forms with a broad milky bloom on the top of each glove, faint contact shadows and a neutral lens. Its light bias is in range, but A's low values reflect a soft top light that the eye reads as real.
pairs.fix: Replace the milky glow on top of the gloves with a soft leather sheen. Add dark shadows on the floor under and beside each glove, and turn the shadow side slightly cool.

pairs.difference: A: firm directional light with bright edge highlights along the yellow blades, a hard dark lower edge and a clear dark turn on the foot pockets, though it runs above the real range on all three fields. B: soft airbrushed fins with no core shadow, the blades nearly one mid value, a pale rim all around and a bright glow behind. The numbers lean against this call, so it rests on the eye.
pairs.fix: Give each fin a clear light side and dark side with a shadow running along the raised ribs. Remove the pale outline glow and the bright halo behind the fins.

pairs.difference: A: posts turn gently as soft cylinders, the planks are evenly lit and the shading is neutral. B: posts and planks drop abruptly to near-black at the waterline, the post throws no shadow onto the deck or life ring, and the lens stays orange and blue, so colour is doing the modelling instead of light.
pairs.fix: Light the post and planks softly with a gentle round turn, not a sudden drop to black. Let the post cast a soft shadow across the deck and onto the life ring.

pairs.difference: A: a clear palm-shaped cast shadow lands on the sand to the right, the trunk turns from a lit left to a darker right, and the fronds have a soft shadow side under the crown. B: the tree has almost no cast shadow, the stones barely ground, and fronds have an inconsistent mix of pale rims on the left and blue on the right.
pairs.fix: Draw a dark palm-shaped shadow on the sand to the right of the trunk, with small shadows under the stones. Light every frond from the same upper-left side, without bright edges.

pairs.difference: A: pillowy bevels with a pale glowing rim running around every edge, so the side plane and front barely separate, plus a soft bloom on the wall. B: flatter faces with crisper corners and a clear directional shadow off the feet, though the front is rather evenly lit and its light bias of 0.106 is low. Both are weak on direction.
pairs.fix: Remove the bright edge glow. Make the faces flat with crisp corners, with the side panel clearly darker than the front, and drop a firm dark shadow into the inside of the locker.

pairs.difference: A: consistent light, with the platform, posts and ladder all throwing clear shadows across the tile deck and a smooth turn along the slide's walls. B: the slide interior is bleached near-white while the outer wall goes dark blue-grey in the lens, the deck shadows are weak, and the green is flat. Its light bias of 0.149 is below the real cards.
pairs.fix: Bring one clear light from the upper left. Let the slide's inner channel turn smoothly from light to mid green with no bleached white patch, and cast clear shadows from the platform, posts and ladder onto the tiles.

pairs.difference: A: a controlled soft top sheen, crisp inset grooves shaded on one side and small soft shine on the earbuds. B: a puffy body with broad milky light on the top and a thick dark core along the lower edge that wraps like a pillow. The lens shows a blurred glow under the body.
pairs.fix: Make the body a firmer rounded box with one soft sheen on top and only a thin shadow along the lower edge. Remove the milky glow, and add small crisp shadows inside the button grooves.

pairs.difference: A: flat paper planes, with gentle shading along the flap folds, thin shadows between photos and little height. B: the envelope is inflated, with a bright rolled rim along every edge and a soft dark underside, so paper reads like moulded plastic, and a bright halo sits behind it.
pairs.fix: Make the envelope flat paper with thin edges and soft shading only along the folds. Remove the bright rim around the edges and the glow behind it, and add thin soft shadows under the photos.

pairs.difference: A: soft even light on the fruit, a gentle sheen on the grapes and a soft shadow under the plate; its light bias of 0.185 is a little low. B: glossy droplets and hot specular points scattered across the plate and fruit, dark crevices between the grapes and berries, and a faint plate shadow. The difference is slight.
pairs.fix: Use fewer water drops and softer shine on the fruit. Open up the dark gaps between the fruit, and place a clear soft shadow under the plate on one side.

pairs.difference: A: dappled ivy cast shadows fall across the upper door and frame, with the left jamb in shade, so light clearly comes from one side. B: flat frontal light with leaves barely shadowing the wall or door. Its light bias of 0.045 is far below the real cards, so only the wreath has a small drop shadow.
pairs.fix: Bring sunlight from the upper right so the ivy throws dappled leaf shadows across the door and frame. Darken one side of the door recess and give the wreath a clear offset shadow.

pattern: Generated cards still light form softly from the front, in four ways. Heroes look inflated, with pale rims around every edge and milky bloom on top instead of a clear lit plane meeting a darker cool side plane at a firm corner. Shadow sides stay warm and shallow, or colour carries the modelling. A bright halo or spotlight pool sits behind the hero. Cast and contact shadows are weak or missing, so objects do not sit under one consistent light.
